newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields drop, gear up for benign CPI.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields drop, gear up for benign CPI.

text.p: *Australian bond yields fell to their lowest level since late February as Tuesday's low pay award by the AIRC, benign CPI expectations and rally in U.S. bonds fuelled a month-long rally.
*March quarter CPI due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond yields fell to their lowest level since late February, extending this month's strong rally as a combination of factors propelled the futures market higher, traders said.

The market remains upbeat on expectations of a benign March quarter CPI outcome at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), along with Tuesday's low pay award by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission, and gained a further leg from a rally in U.S. bonds.
Forecasts centre on a headline CPI rise of just 0.1 percent for the quarter, bringing annual inflation to 1.2 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
The policy sensitive underlying rate is seen up 0.4 percent for year-on-year growth of 2.1 percent.

"The market has built in a lot for these numbers, so there is a risk of disappointment if they come out much above expectations," one trader said. "You could see the yield curve fall 10 basis points."

However, a result at the low end of forecasts -- a 0.1 percent quarterly fall for headline and 0.2 percent for underlying -- would see the advance continue and key resistance at 93.34/35 on the three-year bond futures contract tested, he added.
The market saw active two-way flows in after hours trading and built on the advance following the AIRC's A$10 per week pay award to low paid workers, which was at the low end of expectations.

The AIRC said that the award would add only 0.34 percent to average weekly ordinary time earnings, and analysts say this will keep this measure well within the Reserve Bank's 4.0 to 4.5 percent comfort zone.
The news also added fire to growing specualtion that the Reserve Bank now has scope to ease policy again if it feels that the economic recovery needs a further boost.

The market outperformaned the rally in U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday, which were buoyed by a solid two-year note auction and hopes of an agreement on a balanced budget between the Clinton administration and Republican leaders. Long N.Z. debt held its ground amid some talk of switching from Australia.
